(basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. ==High school career== Boston originally attended [[Norcross High School]] in [[Norcross, Georgia]] before transferring to [[Sierra Canyon School]] in the [[Los Angeles]] neighborhood of [[Chatsworth, Los Angeles|Chatsworth]] in 2019. He played alongside [[LeBron James]]'s son [[Bronny James]] and [[Dwyane Wade]]'s son [[Zaire Wade]].{{cite news|first=Tarek|last=Fattal|title=Sierra Canyon basketball adds second 5-star recruit in less than 24 hours, BJ Boston from Georgia|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/07/19/sierra-canyon-basketball-adds-second-5-star-recruit-in-less-than-24-hours-bj-boston-from-georgia/|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Daily News]]|date=July 19, 2019|access-date=February 21, 2020}} In his final season at Norcross, he averaged 18.4 points and 5.4 rebounds per game.{{cite web | last=Friedlander | first=David | title=Reports: Norcross 5-star Brandon Boston joining star-studded LA powerhouse Sierra Canyon | website=Gwinnett Daily Post | date=July 19, 2019| url=https://www.gwinnettdailypost.com/sports/prep/reports-norcross-5-star-brandon-boston-joining-star-studded-la-powerhouse-sierra-canyon/article_751ac0f3-f0aa-527c-bde9-70959eb1a696.html | access-date=2025-12-06}} He was selected to play in the [[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]. He was also selected to play in the 2020 [[Jordan Brand Classic]].{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Roberts|title=Jordan Brand Classic rosters are out. How many Kentucky basketball recruits made it?|url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-recruiting/article240289151.html|work=[[Lexington Herald Leader]]|date=February 14, ==College career== In his college debut on November 25, 2020, Boston posted 15 points and seven rebounds in an 81–45 win over [[2020–21 Morehead State Eagles men's basketball team|Morehead State]].{{cite news|title=No. 10 Kentucky rolls past Morehead State 81-45 in opener|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401258857|work=[[ESPN]]|date=November 26, 2020|access-date=June 18, 2021}} He scored 21 points in the season finale win against [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]]. As a freshman, he averaged 11.5 points and 4.5 rebounds per game. On March 20, 2021, Boston declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|title=Kentucky's Brandon Boston Jr. becomes third Wildcat to declare for NBA draft|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31101753|work=[[ESPN]]|date=March 20, 2021|access-date=June 23, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles / Agua Caliente / Ontario Clippers (2021–2024)=== Boston was selected in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] with the 51st pick by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], then traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] via the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|title=Pelicans acquire Valančiūnas and Graham in three-team trade with Grizzlies and Hornets|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-jonas-valanciunas-devonte-graham-three-team-trade-memphis-grizzlies-charlotte-hornets|website=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2021|access-date=November 11, 2023}}{{cite web|title=Pelicans complete trade with Clippers|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-complete-trade-clippers|website=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2021|access-date=November 11, 2023}} Boston was assigned to the Clippers' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|Agua Caliente Clippers]], for their G League season-opener. Boston helped the since-relocated Ontario Clippers win the [[2022–23 NBA G League season#Winter Showcase|G League Winter Showcase]] championship in 2022, earning Showcase Cup MVP honors after scoring 21 points in the final.{{cite news|first=Kyle|last=Irving|title=2022 G League Winter Showcase roundup: Results, stats, top performances, prize money from tournament|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/2022-g-league-winter-showcase-roundup-results-stats-top-performances-prize-money/easdehcrwe8zjcvvrvdjqxsz|work=[[Sporting News]]|date=December 23, 2022|access-date=December 23, 2022}} On August 8, 2024, Boston signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]],{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Spurs Sign Brandon Boston Jr.|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/08/spurs-brandon-boston-jr-agree-to-contract.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=August 8, 2024|access-date=September 1, 2024}}{{cite web|author=NathanBeighle|title=Brandon Boston Jr. signs with the San Antonio Spurs|url=https://www.aseaofblue.com/2024/8/9/24217107/brandon-boston-jr-san-antonio-spurs-la-clippers|website=ASeaOfBlue.com|date=August 9, 2024|access-date=August 17, 2024}} but was waived on October 19.{{cite web|author=sasmcasey|title=Spurs Announce 2024-25 Opening Night Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-announce-2024-25-opening-night-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2024–2025)=== On October 21, 2024, Boston was claimed off waivers by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], who later converted his deal into a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans claim Brandon Boston Jr. off waivers|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/brandon-boston-jr-waivers-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-moves-october-21-2024|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2024|access-date=October 22, 2024}} On February 26, 2025, the Pelicans signed Boston to a standard, two-year contract.{{Cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans converting Brandon Boston Jr. to a standard two-year contract|url=https://www.nationofblue.com/new-orleans-pelicans-converting-brandon-boston-jr-to-a-standard-two-year-contract/|access-date=February 27, 2025|website=nationofblue.com|language=en}} He made 42 appearances (10 starts) for New Orleans during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 10.7 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 2.2 assists. On April 28, it was announced that Boston had undergone [[arthroscopy|arthroscopic surgery]] on his left ankle.{{Cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans center Kelly Olynyk, guard Brandon Boston undergo surgery|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/pelicans/pelicans-kelly-olynyk-brandon-boston-undergo-surgery/article_7245346d-82f9-4789-9485-3987265d8403.html|access-date=May 6, 2025|website=nola.com|language=en}} === Fenerbahçe (2025–2026) === [[File:Brandon Boston 11 Fenerbahçe Basketbol Euroleague 20251001 (1) (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Boston with [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] in 2025]] On August 4, 2025, Boston signed with Turkish powerhouse [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web |date=2025-08-04 |title=Brandon Boston Jr. Fenerbahçe Beko’da |url=https://fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2025/8/brandon-boston-jr-fenerbahce-beko-da |access-date=2025-08-04 |website=Fenerbahce.org |language=tr}} On 1 October 2025, he made his [[EuroLeague]] debut against [[Paris Basketball]] in a 96-77 victory with 5 points, 3 rebounds and 1 steal in 8.4 mins.{{Cite web |date=2025-10-01 |title=Son Şampiyon Fenerbahçe Beko, EuroLeague’e galibiyetle başladı |url=https://fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2025/9/son-sampiyon-fenerbahce-beko-euroleague-e-galibiyetle-basladi |access-date=2025-10-02 |website=Fenerbahce.org |language=tr}} On 7 December 2025, in a [[2025–26 Basketbol Süper Ligi]] away match against [[Merkezefendi Belediyesi Denizli Basket|Yukatel Merkezefendi Basket]], Brandon Boston Jr. tallied season-high 21 points, 7 rebounds and 1 assist in 27 mins.{{Cite web |date=2025-12-07 |title=Brandon Boston Jr. scores 21 points to extend Fenerbahce’s streak |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/tbl/1904034/fenerbahce-at-merkezefendi-bsl-round-10-recap-turkiye/ |access-date=2025-12-15 |website=Eurohoops |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2021}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A.
